round: architect-scoped round: every person's decision reaches the architect it is owed to and the controller, never lost (told twice is the lesser fault); the model reaches every transition the daemon makes; RootHears leaves main's resume paths unchanged
accepted: Review 5712285709's four findings and its comment are fixed: DropCatchUps keeps a catch-up under a live lease (the 30 s lease is renewed every 10 s, so a lapse mid-publish is a double telling, never a loss); asksRoot keeps a held root task from askFirst and foreign-turn confirmation; the superseded receipt timeout hands over through supersededKept; an orphan carrying its run takes its subtree's kept rows (MoveKeptDecisions) and its held ones (ReKeepDeliveredDecisions); the KeptToldSource comment names the Published key.

RootHears/asksRoot leave main's resume paths effectively unchanged: ResumeAwaitedRoot and a fresh start carry no Kept, so rootTask returns them unchanged, and after a restart the shim's delivery-id dedupe (shimwire/dedupe.go) answers a re-send of the same id without a second prompt.
currentRootTask retires nothing it should send: an approval pair alone is kept in the rewritten text, and '{}' maps to no Kept.

keyFindings.description: readmit moves and re-keeps a child's subtree decisions only when orphan := carry && !IsTreeRoot. A hand-over or orphan without its run (an Admitted child a blocker holds, which linger hands over; a parked child a person sets todo) still sets stored.Tree = stored.Key. Its rows stay under the old root, and rootTask then drops its marks from the old root's held task with nothing re-kept, so the decision is lost. linger's handedOverSubtrees counts that child and logs Info 'goes to the child' instead of the Warn, so the change removes its own alarm. Move on every tree change (oldTree != stored.Key), whatever carry is.

A root waiting for its slot keeps a person's decision under its own key (RelayKept), and the controller is not told. If admission then adopts that queued root into a live tree (workflow/adopt.go Engine.Adopt, through adoptQueuedRoots or release_children), its tree changes and no start or catch-up ever names the row. Both the architect and the controller miss the decision. Adopt must move those rows to the tree's root and, when that root hears, queue a catch-up as HandOverKept does.

subtree walks every descendant in the old tree, but linger hands over every unfinished member, grandchildren included, each into a tree of its own. If child C's re-admission runs before grandchild G's, C takes G's rows and G's own architect never hears them. The outcome depends on event order. Stop the walk at a descendant that holds its own hand-over fence, with one shared walk for admit.subtree and linger.handedOverSubtrees so the close's Warn/Info split stays true.

notFindings: The duplicated newer-wins upsert in MoveKeptDecisions and AddParkedDecision, and parked_decision_test.go passing 1,000 lines, are maintainability items, not faults.
implement.json's propertyModelGaps text is stale (a child's decision kept under its root; nothing retires a claim). It is a handoff record, not shipped code; the round's fix should update it.
modelGaps: The property model has one root and one child that always carries its run. It has no hand-over without the run, no orphan made by a person's todo, no grandchild hand-over, no adoption and no tree close, which is why it reached none of the three findings.
